newsitem.title: FRANCE: FOCUS-Rhone-Poulenc profit up in quarter. [CORRECTED 13:10 GMT]
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Rhone-Poulenc profit up in quarter. [CORRECTED 13:10 GMT]

text.p: French chemicals and drugs group Rhone-Poulenc reported a 13 percent rise in net income for the third quarter on Friday, prompting its shares to hit a high for the year.

The shares peaked at 145.90 francs in early trading, compared with a previous close of 142.50, and traded around 145 francs by 0850 GMT. The CAC-40 leading share index made a small overall retreat of around 0.20 percent.
The group said the recent withdrawal of its albumin products could incur charges of 100 to 200 million francs in 1996.

It reported net income of 756 million francs ($147 million) versus 669 million at the same stage last year and an operating profit of 2.054 billion francs versus 1.828 billion. Net sales were 20.468 billion francs versus 19.621 billion.

It took a charge of 81 million francs after announcing on October 10 that it was recalling albumin products made by its U.S. unit Rhone-Poulenc Rorer in a joint venture with Hoechst as a precaution against bacterial infection.
The company expects total charges in 1996, including this 81 million, of 100-200 million francs for the withdrawal, finance director Jean-Pierre Tirouflet told a news conference.
Tirouflet reaffirmed the total effect on net profits of the recall by the Centeon joint venture with Hoechst would reduce 1996 net income by six to seven percent compared to analysts' forecasts.

Asked to comment on a forecast of 2.75 billion (corrects from 2.50 billion) francs for 1996 net profits, Tirouflet said: "I have lower forecasts in my head." Rhone-Poulenc later clarified that Tirouflet was not making an official company forecast.
(Corrects reference figure and makes clear Tirouflet was not giving a company forecast)
"Excluding this charge, net income would have progressed by 25.1 percent," Rhone-Poulenc said in a statement with its third quarter results.
"This progress is a consequence of an improvement in results in the pharmaceutical, animal health and agro businesses," it said of the latest results.

Rhone said the agro sector recorded a 14.7 percent increase in sales and a 54.9 percent rise in its profit contribution due to a good economic climate in the global market and the successful marketing of new products, especially Fipronil.
In chemicals and the fibres and polymers divisions, a rise in volumes failed to compensate for falling prices.
Operating profit on the chemicals side was relatively steady at 281 million francs versus 278 million, while in fibres and polymers it took a dive to 115 million from 248 million.

The company said it had completed sales of non-strategic assets to the tune of six billion francs by September 30 and that its net debt-to-equity ratio had fallen to 0.63 versus 0.72 at the end of 1995.
Tirouflet said Rhone expected assets sales to reach seven to nine billion francs by the end of the year. ($1=5.141 French Franc)
